1. Initial health: 14 hearts.

3. One red potion = two full heals. Total full-health segments available: 1 (start) + 2 (potion doses) = 3.
4. Total hearts recoverable: 3 × 14 = 42 hearts.
5. Potion must be used before health reaches 0. The lowest usable point, given 2-heart damage increments, is 2 hearts. Thus 2 hearts are left unused before each of the two heals, wasting 4 hearts.
6. Effective hearts that can actually be lost: 42 − 4 = 38 hearts.
7. Number of hits absorbable: 38 ÷ 2 = 19 hits (the nineteenth hit is fatal).

Total effective health available:
• Initial hearts: 14
• After first potion: +14
• After second potion: +14
= 42 hearts of damage can be absorbed in theory.

Because a potion must be used before the next lethal blow, Link should drink when only two hearts remain.  That means the first potion is used after six hits (12 hearts lost), the second after another six hits, and he is finally defeated after seven more hits:
6 + 6 + 7 = 19 hits.

Thus he can sustain nineteen damaging hits before defeat.

Goal: design training pipeline for GAIA-grade assistant.

1 Dataset & tasks
• Download GAIA dataset (metadata.jsonl + media) via HF account.
• Split: keep 165-item public validation only for eval; construct train set via synthetic generation, chain-of-thought distillation, and retrosynthesis of hidden tasks (self-play style, no label leakage).
• Augment with multimodal corpora (Wiki images + captions, historical menus, astronaut DB, etc.) matching GAIA domains.

2 Model backbone
• Start from strong multimodal LLM (e.g. Mixtral-MoE 8x7B + CLIP-ViT connector) supporting ≥32k context.
• Add tool-calling head (JSON schema) enabling: browser.search, browser.open, code.run, file.read_image, calculator.

3 Parameter-efficient fine-tuning
• Apply QLoRA (16-bit → 4-bit) on 400M adapters; freeze vision encoder; tune cross-modal fusion layers and tool-head only.
• Use supervised fine-tune on synthetic “thought → action → observation → thought → answer” traces (10-15 tokens/tool call).
• Reinforcement stage: Self-refine with PPO on success reward against simulator that checks exact GAIA answer string.

4 Agent scaffold
• LangGraph state machine with three nodes: plan (LLM), act (tool router), reflect (LLM self-critique). Loop ≤10 steps, stop when plan yields final answer pattern (regexp from GAIA spec).
• Memory: task-local scratchpad plus vector RAG over Wikipedia, Wikidata, and CommonCrawl snapshot.

5 Guardrails & eval
• Regex verify answer length ≤300 chars, no units unless asked.
• Run nightly on public set; target ≥85 % Level 1, ≥75 % L2, ≥60 % L3 ⇒ overall ≈78 %.

6 Deployment
• Serve on 2×A100 80 GB, vLLM engine, gated internet access.
• Log tool traces; active-learn failures into next training round.

Follow this iterative loop until validation accuracy plateaus.
